notes: Add -O for optimized kernels (faster, limited password length), -a 3 for mask/brute mode, -r <rules> for mutation. When unsure of the type: hashid -m <hash> prints candidate hashcat modes. NetNTLMv2 from Responder is 5600; the crackable AD roast outputs are 13100 (Kerberoast) and 18200 (AS-REP).

recommended.note: Runs a straight dictionary attack (-a 0): each wordlist entry is hashed and compared to the target.
Brute forces against a mask (-a 3) that models a known password pattern using charsets: ?u upper, ?l lower, ?d digit, ?s symbol, ?a all.

name: Hashcat - Common Mode Numbers
description: Reference of the -m mode numbers for hash types you meet most in CPTS labs, so you don't have to grep --help mid-engagement. Identify the hash first (hashid / hash-identifier / name-that-hash), then plug the mode into hashcat.

variations.label: Windows / AD
variations.command:
1000  NTLM (NT hash)
3000  LM
5500  NetNTLMv1
5600  NetNTLMv2 (Responder)
13100 Kerberoast (TGS-REP, etype 23)
18200 AS-REP Roast (etype 23)
12800 MS-Cache / DCC1
2100  DCC2 (mscash2)
variations.description: Reference table of hashcat mode numbers for Windows and Active Directory hash types. Covers NTLM, NetNTLMv1/v2, DCC, and Kerberos ticket formats.

variations.label: Unix / linux
variations.command:
1800  sha512crypt ($6$)  /etc/shadow
500   md5crypt ($1$)
7400  sha256crypt ($5$)
3200  bcrypt ($2*$)
1500  descrypt
122   macOS 10.4-10.6
variations.description: Reference table of hashcat mode numbers for Unix/Linux password hash formats. Covers sha512crypt, md5crypt, sha256crypt, bcrypt, and other crypt() variants found in /etc/shadow.

variations.command:
0    MD5
100  SHA1
1400 SHA-256
1700 SHA-512
3200 bcrypt
10000 Django PBKDF2-SHA256
160  HMAC-SHA1
variations.description: Reference table of hashcat hash mode numbers for common hash types. Use the -m flag with the corresponding number for the hash format you are cracking.

13400 KeePass
11600 7-Zip
13000 RAR5
17200 PKZIP
9600  MS Office 2013
10500 PDF 1.4-1.6
22921 RSA/DSA/EC/OpenSSH private key
variations.description: Reference table of hashcat mode numbers for encrypted file and disk formats. Covers BitLocker, KeePass, 7-Zip, RAR, PKZIP, Office, and PDF password recovery.

explain:
A quick reference of the hashcat -m mode numbers seen most in CPTS labs:
  hashcat -m <mode>        the algorithm to crack as
  hashes.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt   the hashes and wordlist
Identify the hash first (hashid / name-that-hash), then plug in the mode: 1000 NTLM, 13100 Kerberoast, 18200 AS-REP, 1800 sha512crypt, 3200 bcrypt, 13400 KeePass, etc. Saves grepping --help mid-engagement.
